title: Terraform-driven upgrade choreographer for private control plane (drift-safe, tenant-fenced canaries)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a Terraform-native 'upgrade choreographer' pattern and associated modules to run sequenced control-plane upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments. The choreographer will apply drift-safe plans, coordinate tenant-fenced canaries, run preflight health checks, and automate safe promotion or rollback decisions. This ticket covers design, prototype module, and an end-to-end staging rehearsal (no customer-facing production changes) to validate the approach.
acceptance_criteria: New terraform module 'redwood_upgrade_choreographer' lives in infra-modules and exposes a declarative canary rollout plan as inputs.
Choreographer can run a 3-wave canary against a staging VPC cluster: initial smoke (2 tenants), expanded canary (10% tenants), full promotion.
Automated preflight collects health metrics and gates promotion using configurable thresholds (p95 latency, RPC error rate, reconcile duration).
If any gate fails, choreographer marks the wave failed and provides an easy 'terraform apply --target=rollback' plan and human-facing runbook to revert.
All changes are covered by unit + integration tests and a documented runbook in Confluence with links to dashboards and run commands.
design_notes: Principle: keep control-plane changes atomic and reversible. Use terraform state-locking + plan cache to ensure we never 'apply' blind promotions.
Module shape: inputs = [target_version, waves (list of {tenants_selector, traffic_fraction, preflight_checks}), timeout_seconds, rollback_policy]. Outputs = [wave_statuses, last_plan_sha].

Drift-safety: choreographer first runs a dry-run 'plan' against each target tenant subset; if diff > threshold (e.g. more than resource replacements or unknown changes), abort and surface drift report.

Execution model: choreography runs as a controller binary (single-run CLI) that invokes terraform in a guarded environment (CI runner with state credentials). This avoids long-running terraform processes inside control plane.
Compatibility: rely on existing version-contract manifest for control-plane APIs; choreographer validates CRD versions and API compatibility before wave 1.
rollout_plan: Preflight: generate per-tenant plan files and a consolidated diff report saved to artifact store.
Wave 0 - smoke: apply to 2 isolated test tenants in staging VPC; run health checks for 30m.
Wave 1 - canary: expand to 10% tenant subset (configurable) with traffic mirroring and 2h observation window.
Wave 2 - promote: full promotion for remaining tenants with rolling pause points every N batches to check telemetry.
Post-promote: 48h elevated monitoring, automated canary scoring, and an automated follow-up job that re-runs reconciliation to catch latent drift.
health_checks: Service-level: control-plane /health, /ready endpoints must return 200 and respond within 200ms p95 under 99th percentile load test.
API correctness: run end-to-end CRUD flows for tenancy objects and assert no schema/regression errors.
Latency SLO guard: p95 API latency increase <= 20% vs baseline for the canary group.
Error guard: 5xx rate must remain below 0.5% and no crashloops in pods for 30 min.
KV cache check: KV cache miss rate should not exceed baseline + 10% during promotion window.
Reconcile window: any controller reconciliations taking > 3x baseline flagged as high-risk.
terraform_changes: Add new module 'redwood/upgrade_choreographer' (semver 0.1.0) which wraps plan/apply workflows and emits plan artifacts.
Introduce an 'upgrade_plan' S3/GCS artifact schema that includes per-tenant plan SHA, resource-change counts, and a machine-readable risk score.
Extend existing controlplane module with a 'version_contract' input that enumerates compatible component versions to prevent mismatched promotions.
Ensure remote state locking and encrypted state at rest; choreographer CI runner must assume a limited-perm service account scoped only to state operations and apply targets listed in the plan.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terraform-module terratest suites validating input permutations, plan generation, and outputs.
Integration: run choreographer in vpc-staging (isolated) and execute smoke + canary waves with synthetic traffic (locust).
Chaos test: simulated API failures during wave 1 to ensure gating logic triggers rollback and leaves state consistent.
Load test: run 60-minute ramp to replicate production-ish token rates while measuring ballistic metrics used in gates.
Compliance test: verify that KMS/HSM-encrypted state is used for private customer keys and that audit logs are emitted for all plane changes.
